transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm not wasting your time, it's probably just me being a little scattered lately, but... well, what finally made me ask for help is that I just keep forgetting these little things. Things I normally handle without any problem at all. 

Like, um, forgetting to return phone calls—which is really embarrassing since I'm a secretary, I usually always stay on top of that—or forgetting to turn in a registration form, or even just remembering to stop for a quick errand on the way home. It's nothing terrible, I know, and I'm still getting by, but it's just not like me to drop the ball on the little things. Does that... does that make sense as a reason to come in?
About how long ago did you first start noticing these changes in your memory?

Um, well... I guess it's been about 15 months or so? Give or take a little. I started taking an evening certificate program around then, just to try and learn some new skills for work. And I think ever since I added that to my schedule, keeping my attention on things and staying organized has just gotten... noticeably harder to manage. 

I mean, I know anyone would get a little forgetful when they're busy, so I really hope I'm not making a mountain out of a molehill here. But that's when it really started standing out to me. Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Growing up as a child or teenager, did you ever struggle with paying attention or staying organized in school?

Um... well, I guess if I really think back... yeah, a little bit. I mean, I wasn't a bad student or anything, I promise! I always tried really hard to be good and follow the rules. 

But, um, even back in elementary school, I was kind of that kid who... you know, forgot permission slips, or somehow lost my finished homework at the bottom of my backpack. And my mom or my teachers usually had to sit with me and remind me, step by step, to actually finish my projects. I feel a little silly admitting that, because they were always so patient with me and I really wanted to do a good job for them. 

Does that... does that answer what you were asking? I hope that's not too unusual to hear.

{"intent": "Assess for core symptoms of generalized anxiety to differentiate GAD from ADHD", "question": "Do you often find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different everyday things

Um, well... I wouldn't say I worry *excessively*, no. I mean, I care about doing a good job and making sure things are taken care of, but I don't think I'm, like, a nervous wreck or anything. 

I might stress a little bit if I know I forgot something important at work, just because I don't want to let my boss down, but I think that's pretty normal, right? I try really hard not to let things get to me too much. I hope that's the right kind of answer... I just wouldn't want you to think I'm overly anxious when it's really just me trying to keep all my ducks in a row. Does that make sense?
Over the past several months, have you been feeling persistently down, depressed, or hopeless?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I definitely get frustrated with myself sometimes when I mess up or forget things, but I don't feel depressed or hopeless. 

I actually really like my life, and I try to stay positive! I just want to figure out how to be a bit more organized so I can do better at my job and my classes. I hope it doesn't seem like I'm complaining too much about things. I'm really okay overall, just... a little scattered lately. Is that what you meant?
